title: Mint the pro-rata-ratio lesson as its own id (folded into L-214 at the 52/52 cap)
why: register cap -- the lessons register was at 52/52 entries during the Release 1 window, so a genuinely distinct lesson was folded into L-214 rather than minting a new id; archiving to make room is a deliberate cross-reference-checked process that should not be rushed during a release
notes: The folded rule is separate and expensive: a pro-rata ratio must be derived from the SPECIFIC stored row being reversed, never a sum across the parent entity's rows. The class hides because the CLOSING operation books the exact remaining and absorbs the difference, so the total always reconciles and the error surfaces only as filing-PERIOD attribution, and only when a partial straddles a boundary. Cost of leaving it folded: the register's value is that a future session can find a rule by its own id and citation, and a distinct lesson living inside another entry is materially less discoverable. Action: archive the least-cited fully-guarded entry properly, then mint this as its own id. Rationale for the interim fold is recorded in .claude/lessons/_meta.json note.

title: Code-map catch-up: 42 code commits merged to master since the last map refresh (a76e2e2c..c73b0897)
why: release throughput -- every lane merged under Bookkeeping Option B, which defers the map entry to a docs-only follow-up after the code PR lands; the follow-ups have not kept pace with the Release 1 merge rate, so the debt is now 42 commits across api, web, mobile and packages
notes: Range a76e2e2c..c73b0897, 2026-09-20 to 2026-09-22, spanning #1048 through #1212. Surfaced by the stop gate firing on a docs-only branch off master: the gate compares code commits against the last .claude/code-map/ change, so the debt is inherited by every branch cut from master and every lane now trips it regardless of whether that lane mapped its own work. Not any one lane's to absorb -- mapping 42 other PRs from outside their context is how a map gets confidently wrong. Owned by the landing coordinator, which works from a master tree and owns bookkeeping. Note that the gate's own remedy text (the Bookkeeping-Follow-Up trailer) is what allowed the debt to accumulate silently: it is per-PR and has no aggregate ceiling, so consider whether the gate should also fail on a backlog depth rather than only on the presence of a trailer.
